title: Affordable rental tax subclass and road salt advocacy
subtitle: Also: paramedic and transit budget changes, graffiti options, staff compensation review, committee appointments, and community award presentations.
overview: Council adopted an optional property tax subclass for affordable rental housing in the multi-residential and new multi-residential classes, effective January 1, 2026 {{vote:m12}}. The discount is to be set at 35 per cent when 2026 tax policy comes forward in spring. Council also asked the Mayor to write to the province seeking tax relief for homeowners on social assistance, grant funding for municipalities that adopt the subclass, and matching education tax discounts.

Council urged the province to develop limited liability legislation for winter maintenance contractors, along with standard best practices and an expert advisory committee on salt pollution {{vote:m16}}. Guelph relies on groundwater for drinking water, so salt reaching aquifers is a local concern.

Through the consent report, Council approved second-quarter budget adjustments, including added paramedic compensation funding and earlier ambulance purchases {{vote:m9}}. It also directed staff to report on graffiti options by the end of the first quarter of 2026 and to fold audit recommendations on facilities cleaning into workplans.

After a closed session, Council voted in open session on staff compensation review changes and on appointments to two advisory committees. It also appointed a councillor to The Elliott board and the Well Interference Committee, and presented city medals to local athletes.

decisions.detail: Council adopted the optional affordable rental housing subclass for multi-residential and new multi-residential properties from January 1, 2026, with a 35 per cent discount to be set in the 2026 tax policy.

decisions.item: Letter on tax relief for social assistance homeowners
decisions.detail: The Mayor will ask the province to consider property tax relief for homeowners on Ontario Disability Support Program and Ontario Works, with copies to several bodies.

decisions.item: Letters seeking provincial grants and education tax match
decisions.detail: The Mayor will ask the province for grant funding for municipalities adopting the subclass and for matching education property tax discounts.

decisions.item: Road salt and limited liability advocacy
decisions.detail: Council urged the province to create limited liability legislation and standard practices for snow and ice contractors, and to fund an expert advisory committee, while committing to keep reducing the City's salt use.

Council approved capital adjustments, added paramedic compensation funding shared with the County, advanced ambulance and electric bus charging budgets to 2025, and created a Queen Street sewer project.
Staff were directed to update the list of comparator municipalities used for compensation comparisons, including Council remuneration {{vote:m4}}.

decisions.item: Benefits survey and total compensation reviews
decisions.detail: Staff will survey the competitiveness of non-union employee benefits and move to total compensation reviews, covering pay and benefits, every four years.
Councillor Hauser was appointed to the Board of Trustees of The Elliott and the Well Interference Committee for terms ending November 15, 2026.

debate: On the tax subclass, the mover said the province should help municipalities adopt the discount without shifting costs onto other taxpayers, and should match it on education taxes to encourage more affordable rentals.

On relief for homeowners on social assistance, one councillor supported the request, pointing to the existing seniors tax program as a model and to worries about housing stability for people on fixed incomes.

A delegate from a water advocacy group said road salt is a toxic pollutant that builds up in fresh water and that fear of slip-and-fall claims drives contractors to over-salt. The delegate asked Council to back provincial action.

Councillors asked what limited liability means. The mover said it would cap claims against contractors who show due diligence. Staff said they could not speak to liability without legal staff present, and the memo clarified the focus is private contractors.

Staff said the City already applies salt based on conditions, has tried alternatives such as beet juice, and is working with the University of Guelph on better measurement. One councillor welcomed the disability community's inclusion in the advisory committee.
